artworks.title: Plate Number 174. Running and jumping with skipping rope
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequential motion study featuring 24 black and white frames arranged in three rows and four columns. Each frame captures a single moment in time, depicting a figure in various stages of movement. The background features a simple lined pattern. The lighting and shadows highlight the fluidity of the subject's actions across the frames.

artworks.title: Plate Number 175. Crossing brook on stepping-stones with a fishing pole and can
artworks.description: The image shows a series of photographs of a woman walking backward with a pail. She is seen stepping over objects, balancing with one foot raised, holding a pail in one hand and a whip in the other. The woman's hair is styled up and her face is not clearly visible due to motion and distance. She is wearing a short, wrapped garment reaching her knees. The background has a lined backdrop typical of motion study photography, suggesting an outdoor setting with sunlight and shadows.

artworks.title: Plate Number 176. Crossing brook on stepping-stones with fishing pole and a basket
artworks.description: The image shows a sequence of black and white photographs capturing a nude woman in motion. She is walking, carrying a small bucket and a long stick, possibly a fishing rod. The woman's body is visible in each frame as she moves over stones on the ground. Her long hair is worn loose down her back. The background features a grid-like pattern, suggesting a wire fence or screen. The ground is scattered with round stones. There are no visible jewelry on the woman.

artworks.title: Plate Number 177. Crossing brook on stepping-stones with fishing pole and a basket
artworks.description: The image shows three rows of photographs depicting a person walking in motion. The person is shown from different angles, with long hair styled in braids. They are carrying a basket on their back and holding a stick or rod. The background features a wire grid and the ground is uneven with stones.

artworks.title: Plate Number 178. Stepping on and over a trestle
artworks.description: This is a photograph of sequential images capturing a person's movement. The image shows two rows of grid-lined backdrop with a sequence of a nude figure stepping over a stool. Each frame captures a distinct position as the figure progresses through the act of stepping. The lighting highlights the figure against the backdrop. The composition is methodical, almost scientific in its documentation of movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 179. Stepping on and over a rock, a basket on head and right hand raised
artworks.description: This is a series of sequential images capturing motion. The grid of small, sequential photographs depicts an individual carrying a basket on their head while stepping up and moving across the frame. Multiple rows and columns show different positions, providing a sense of movement and progression through space. The series is arranged in a way that gives a cinematic effect, documenting changes in posture and fluid motion. The image is monochromatic, emphasizing movement over color or details.

artworks.title: Plate Number 181. Stepping over a fence
artworks.description: The image shows a series of photographs of a person in motion. The person is stepping over an object, possibly a pole or bar, in various stages of movement. The individual is a woman with her hair tied back and wearing a translucent dress. The photographs capture different angles of the woman as she carefully steps over the obstacle. There are no visible jewelry items on the woman. The background is a lined surface or wall that serves as a neutral backdrop for the subject's motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 182. Crawling on hands and knees
artworks.description: The image shows a sequence of photographs of a person moving on all fours. The individual is captured from side, front, and rear angles. They are positioned on hands and knees, suggesting crawling. The person has short hair pulled back and is not wearing any clothing. The setting appears to be a controlled environment, with a grid-lined backdrop in the side views and a wooden plank on the floor. In the rear view, the same grid backdrop is visible. The setting seems outdoor, with natural light and shadows and a simple, organized background. There are no visible pieces of jewelry or objects being held by the individual.

artworks.title: Plate Number 183. Walking on hands and feet
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series capturing movement. The image is a grid of sequential black-and-white photographs that detail a step-by-step progression of motion. The backdrop features a lined chart. Each frame captures a slightly different position, revealing the fluid transition of motion within a single sequence. The lighting is even, with the focus clearly on the subject of the movement across consecutive stills. This composition conveys a sense of study and observation.

artworks.title: Plate Number 184. Walking on hands and feet
artworks.description: This is a photograph of sequential imagery depicting a nude figure bending over. The image consists of a grid of photographs capturing a series of movements. The grid is made up of three rows, each containing images showing the progressive motion of a figure bending forward. The background features a vertical pattern. The position of the figure changes slightly in each frame, creating a sense of motion. The variation in the figure's posture is systematically documented across the frames, showing the continuous transition of the human form in motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 185. Hopping on left foot
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a human figure in motion captured in multiple sequential frames. Each frame shows the figure at different stages of a movement, captured from three different angles.

artworks.title: Plate Number 187. Dancing (fancy)
artworks.description: This is a set of twelve sequential images showing a figure in flowing fabric posing against a gridded backdrop. The fabric trails elegantly, emphasizing the figure's movement. The grid lines provide a reference for the scale and direction of the movement. Each photograph captures a different moment in the sequence.

artworks.title: Plate Number 188. Dancing (fancy)
artworks.description: This is a series of twelve black-and-white photographs arranged in a grid, with two lines of six photos. The photographs capture a person in a flowing dress dancing in an outdoor setting. The fabric drapes and follows the movement of the person, showcasing delicate and fluid motion. The grid layout highlights the progression and continuity of the dance, as the person is in a different pose in each photograph. The setting appears to be a tiled or paved area with a backdrop of darker tones.

artworks.title: Plate Number 189. Dancing (fancy)
artworks.description: The image depicts a series of 12 frames showing a woman in various dance poses. She is balancing on one leg with the other lifted, arms extended holding a flowing fabric. Her hair is styled in an updo, and she wears a sheer, flowing dress. She is barefoot against a backdrop of parallel lines, with no visible jewelry or objects.

artworks.title: Plate Number 190. Dancing (nautch)
artworks.description: The image shows a series of photographs of a woman in motion. She is standing and walking with her arms raised and hands positioned on or above her head. Her long hair is flowing, and she is wearing a sheer cloth around her lower body, leaving her upper body exposed. The background features vertical lines, possibly part of a door or partition, and the ground is textured like pavement or tiles. The sequence captures the woman in different poses, emphasizing her movement and the flow of the fabric and her hair. There are no visible objects in her hands or jewelry worn.

artworks.title: Plate Number 191. Dancing (fancy)
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of sequential images capturing motion. The image consists of a grid of black and white photographs, each showing different frames in sequence, documenting a motion study.

artworks.title: Plate Number 192. Dancing (fancy)
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence of movement studies. The image consists of a series of black-and-white frames arranged in a grid, each depicting a fluid and graceful movement. The subject is draped in a flowing garment, accentuating the motion. The background features a simple grid pattern. This method was commonly used in the late 19th to early 20th century to study human movement through photography.

artworks.title: Plate Number 193. Dancing (fancy)
artworks.description: This is a photograph sequence showing a figure holding a flowing garment and moving through a series of steps. The images capture different stages of the movement, highlighting the fluid motion of the fabric. The background features a textured wall or backdrop.

artworks.title: Plate Number 194. Dancing
artworks.description: The image consists of a sequence of photographs arranged in two rows. A woman is shown in various stages of movement, with her full body depicted in each frame. The woman is generally upright, captured in different dynamic poses, suggesting motion. Her facial features appear soft and her hair is neat and pulled back. She wears a long, flowing, light-colored dress. The background features a gridded or lined surface, possibly a wall or screen, and the floor is flat and uniform. There are no visible jewelry or objects in the woman's hands.

artworks.title: Plate Number 195. Dancing a waltz
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence showing a figure in motion. The image is a grid composed of multiple frames, each capturing the figure in various stages of motion against a grid-lined background. The subject moves from left to right in the upper row and continues in the lower row, with subtle changes in posture and position from one frame to the next. This systematic documentation highlights the nuances of physical movement through a series of still shots.

artworks.title: Plate Number 197. Man and woman dancing a waltz
artworks.description: This is a series of twenty-four black-and-white photographs showing two people in formal attire engaged in a dance. One of the people is wearing a light-colored dress and the other is wearing a dark suit. The sequence of photographs is arranged in four rows of six photos, and combined they seem to capture the progression of the couple’s movements as they move together. The people are shown in different positions in each frame. The background is plain gray, with their shadows moving across it.

artworks.title: Plate Number 198. Curtesying
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing sequential images capturing the movement of a subject in a long dress. The grid composition consists of two rows with multiple frames, each showing the subject in different positions, indicating motion. The subject wears a detailed Victorian-style outfit with floral patterns and layered garments. The background appears to be a neutral exterior setting with a gridded background that highlights the motion path.

artworks.title: Plate Number 199. Curtesying, a fan in right hand
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white images featuring a figure in motion. The grid displays different stages of the figure transitioning from an upright posture to a bent forward stance while holding a fan. The top row shows side views, and the bottom row shows rear views with variations in arm positions and garment folds. The images capture the study of movement, posture, and bodily nuances in a draped attire setting.

artworks.title: Plate Number 200. Curtseying, kissing hand and turning around
artworks.description: This is an image showing a sequential movement study. It displays a grid of black-and-white frames capturing different phases of a dynamic movement. Each frame shows a side view within a controlled environment with a gridded backdrop. The focus is on the transition of positions, showcasing continuity and fluidity.
